status.en: 131 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 131 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Bandits in Zamfara burned 11 family members, abducted five children and attacked a mosque during Subhi prayer, killing Governor Dauda Lawal's aide and abducting worshippers, while in Plateau gunmen killed herders, farmers and an Operation Rainbow commander, burned seven houses and prompted a curfew. President Tinubu apologized for his absence after the Plateau attack and announced a five-year defence plan as AI-generated disinformation spreads ahead of the election. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter i Zamfara brente 11 familiemedlemmer, bortførte fem barn og angrep en moské under Subhi-bønnen, drepte guvernør Dauda Lawals assistent og bortførte tilbedere, mens skytevåpen i Plateau drepte hyrder, bønder og en kommandør fra Operasjon Rainbow, brente sju hus og førte til en portforbud. President Tinubu beklaget sin fravær etter angrepet i Plateau og kunngjorde en femårs forsvarsplan mens AI-generert desinformasjon sprer seg før valget. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
